Nvidia is facing an investigation by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission into potential accounting issues, Reuters reported Friday, citing two people familiar with the matter, adding to the regulatory challenges confronting the artificial intelligence chipmaker.

SEC enforcement officials are examining possible irregularities in Nvidia’s financial reporting, according to Reuters. The specific accounting practices under investigation remain unclear, and the timing of the inquiry has not been disclosed.

The SEC declined to comment, while Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters.

Nvidia shares fell approximately 13% during Friday’s trading session following the report, according to Reuters, citing LSEG market data. The company’s stock had already been under pressure amid concerns involving its leadership, international business relationships and financial arrangements with artificial intelligence companies.

The investigation follows questions about changes Nvidia made in 2025 to its geographic revenue reporting. Under the revised methodology, the company began allocating sales according to customers’ corporate headquarters rather than their billing addresses.

Nvidia said the adjustment was intended to provide a more accurate representation of the geographic distribution of its business, according to Reuters.

The change eliminated Singapore as a separately reported market in the company’s revenue disclosures.

The Financial Times reported earlier in the week that sales associated with Singapore had accounted for nearly half of Nvidia’s global revenue before the reporting methodology was revised.

Reuters said it could not determine whether the SEC investigation specifically involved the company’s geographic revenue disclosures.

Nvidia’s financial relationships with artificial intelligence companies have also attracted attention as the semiconductor manufacturer expands its involvement in financing AI infrastructure.

The company has participated in investment and financing arrangements involving businesses that purchase its processors and develop computing facilities, according to Reuters.

Related: Nvidia’s $12.9 Billion Hugging Face Deal Draws Justice Department Questions

Those arrangements include investments in AI companies and cloud infrastructure providers, as well as financial guarantees connected to projects using Nvidia technology.

The transactions have prompted questions among some investors about how financing relationships may affect assessments of customer demand and financial exposure.

Reuters reported that SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock said in October that regulators were examining disclosures by artificial intelligence companies to determine whether investors were receiving sufficient information about material financial risks.

During Nvidia’s earnings conference call Tuesday, interim Chief Executive Officer Colette Kress, previously the company’s chief financial officer, indicated that the company planned to become more selective in its financial commitments to the AI sector, according to Reuters.

The accounting inquiry comes amid a leadership controversy involving Nvidia’s former chief executive, Jensen Huang.

Reuters reported that Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship in a November 8 statement following disclosures involving Alice Huang, a former executive associated with Singapore-based technology company Megaspeed.

U.S. authorities suspect Alice Huang of having connections to Chinese intelligence, according to Reuters. China has rejected allegations that she engaged in espionage.

Megaspeed, a customer of Nvidia’s advanced processors, is separately under investigation by U.S. authorities over potential violations of semiconductor export restrictions.

The Justice and Commerce departments disclosed this week that the company had been under examination since 2024 over suspected shipments of advanced AI chips potentially destined for China, Reuters reported.

Megaspeed has said its operations complied with applicable laws and that Alice Huang departed the company in August 2025.

Reuters said it had been unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.

Nvidia is also facing regulatory scrutiny over its acquisition strategy. The U.S. Justice Department has been reviewing the company’s proposed $12.9 billion acquisition of artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face as part of a broader examination of its business practices, Reuters reported in October.
